Let $S$ be a connected smooth quasiprojective complex variety. A **geometric
polarizable rational Hodge variation** on $S$ consists of a finite-rank rational
local system $H$ ([[def-local-system-of-r-modules-and-its-pullback]]), a
continuous pure Hodge decomposition of its fibers, or a finite direct sum of
pure weights, in the sense of [[def-rational-mixed-hodge-structure]], and an
algebraic realization on a nonempty Zariski open $U\subseteq S$: there are
smooth projective morphisms $f_i:X_i\to U$, degrees $m_i$ and integers $r_i$
such that $H|_U$ is a Hodge direct summand of
$$\bigoplus_iR^{m_i}(f_i)_*\mathbb Q(r_i),$$
where $\mathbb Q(r)$ is the Tate structure of
[[def-rational-mixed-hodge-structure]]. A **Hodge direct summand** means the
image of a flat rational idempotent that is a Hodge morphism at every point.

**Given:** The rational vector space $H=\mathbb Q e_0\oplus\mathbb Q e_1$
([[def-rational-mixed-hodge-structure]]), the increasing filtration
$W_{-3}=0$, $W_{-2}=W_{-1}=\mathbb Q e_1$, $W_0=H$ and the decreasing
filtration $F^1H_{\mathbb C}=0$, $F^0H_{\mathbb C}=\mathbb C(e_0+ie_1)$,
$F^{-1}H_{\mathbb C}=H_{\mathbb C}$, with $i\in\mathbb C$ satisfying
$i^2=-1$ and conjugation $\sigma(z)=\bar z$
([[def-complex-numbers-and-arithmetic]]).

[F1] A rational mixed Hodge structure is the datum of a finite increasing $W$ and a finite decreasing $F$ such that on every $\operatorname{Gr}^W_nH_{\mathbb C}$ the induced filtrations are $n$-opposed, i.e. split into the pieces $H^{p,q}_n$ with $\overline{H^{p,q}_n}=H^{q,p}_n$; a morphism preserves $W$ and $F$ ([[def-rational-mixed-hodge-structure]]).

[F2] The Tate structure $\mathbb Q(r)$ is the pure structure of weight $-2r$ with $\mathbb Q(r)_{\mathbb C}=\mathbb C$ concentrated in type $(-r,-r)$; in particular $\mathbb Q(1)$ has weight $-2$ and type $(-1,-1)$, while $\mathbb Q(0)$ has weight $0$ and type $(0,0)$ ([[def-rational-mixed-hodge-structure]]).

[F3] On a graded piece $\operatorname{Gr}^W_nH_{\mathbb C}$ the induced filtration $F$ is the image of $F\cap W_n$ and $\bar F=\sigma(F)$; the summands are $H^{p,q}_n=F^p\operatorname{Gr}^W_n\cap\bar F^q\operatorname{Gr}^W_n$ ([[def-rational-mixed-hodge-structure]]).

(i) Let $K$ be a rational cohomological mixed Hodge complex
([[def-cohomological-mixed-hodge-complex]]). Then for every $n$ the vector
space $H^n(K_{\mathbb Q})$ carries a mixed Hodge structure whose weight
filtration is the shifted image filtration
$W_mH^n(K)=\operatorname{im}(H^n(W_{m-n}K)\to H^n(K))$ and whose Hodge
filtration is the image filtration
$F^pH^n(K_{\mathbb C})=\operatorname{im}(H^n(F^pK_{\mathbb C})\to H^n(K_{\mathbb C}))$.
In the weight spectral sequence $E_1^{p,q}=H^{p+q}(\operatorname{Gr}^W_{-p}K)$
one has $E_1^{p,q}$ pure of weight $q$, the sequence degenerates at $E_2$, and
$\operatorname{Gr}^W_mH^n(K)\cong E_2^{n-m,m}$ compatibly with the Hodge
filtrations. A morphism of cohomological mixed Hodge complexes induces, on
every $H^n$, a morphism of the resulting mixed Hodge structures.

every $w$, $\operatorname{Gr}^W_wK$ has finite-dimensional cohomology, its
differential is strict for the induced $F$, and $H^r(\operatorname{Gr}^W_wK)$

Then $H^\Lambda_2=H_{\mathbb C,-1}(S_2)$ with $T_1^2=-2T_1-1$, i.e.

algebra whose unique simple is $D=\mathbb C$ with $t$ acting as $0$, and whose
regular module is the unique indecomposable projective $P=H^\Lambda_2$. Both
partitions of $2$ have content $\alpha_0+\alpha_1$ in the charge-$0$
convention, so $\alpha_0+\alpha_1$ is the only nonzero block and

one-dimensional modules $S(2)=\mathbb C$ and $S(1,1)=\mathbb C$, both with
trivial underlying action of $t$, and the graded composition series of $P$ is
$0\subset tP\subset P$ with $tP\cong D\{2\}$, so
$$[P]=(1+q^2)[D]\quad\text{in }G_0^{\rm gr}(H^\Lambda_{\alpha_0+\alpha_1}),\qquad [P]\notin\{[D],q^{\pm1}[D],\dots\}.$$

not), the edge degrees of the two shapes are $\deg(S(1,1))=0$ and
$\deg(S(2))=1$, so the graded Specht classes are $[S(1,1)]=[D]$ and
$[S(2)]=q[D]$, and the level-one Fock data give
$G(1,1)=M_{1,1}+qM_{(2)}$ and $G^*(1,1)=(M_{1,1}+qM_{(2)})/(1+q^2)$; hence

$$[P]\longmapsto G(1,1)=M_{1,1}+qM_{(2)}=(1+q^2)G^*(1,1),\qquad [D]\longmapsto G^*(1,1).$$

In branch (CP) of the regime of
[[def-nondegenerate-root-of-unity-level-one-hecke-regime]], for every
$\lambda\in RP_\alpha$ and every partition $\mu$ of content $\alpha$, the
graded decomposition polynomial factors as
$$[S(\mu):D(\lambda)]_q=\sum_{\nu\in RP_\alpha}a_{\lambda,\nu}(q)\,d_{\nu,\mu}(q),$$
where $a_{\lambda,\nu}$ are the adjustment polynomials of
[[def-graded-adjustment-polynomials-in-positive-characteristic]] and
$d_{\nu,\mu}$ the characteristic-independent global-basis transition polynomial
of [[def-level-one-global-basis-transition-polynomials-in-the-symmetric-group-convention]];
equivalently
$[J(\nu)]=[D(\nu)]+\sum_{\lambda\lhd\nu}a_{\lambda,\nu}(q)[D(\lambda)]$. In
particular the characteristic-$p$ decomposition matrix is the product of the
dominance-unitriangular adjustment matrix and the (characteristic-independent)
matrix of global-basis coefficients, and no claim is made that the adjustment
matrix is the identity. Choice is inherited only through the transported
global-basis suppliers.

[F1] The Specht classes realize the standard Fock vectors: $[S(\mu)]$ maps to
$S_\mu$ under $\Psi_{\rm can}^{\rm Hecke}$
([[thm-graded-specht-classes-realize-standard-fock-vectors]]), and
$S_\mu=\sum_{\nu\in RP_\alpha}d_{\nu,\mu}(q)D_\nu$ in the upper family
([[lem-standard-fock-vectors-expand-in-the-upper-global-basis]]), with the
transition polynomials of
[[def-level-one-global-basis-transition-polynomials-in-the-symmetric-group-convention]].

[F2] The reduced modules satisfy
$\Psi_{\rm can}^{\rm Hecke}([J(\nu)])=D_\nu$ over the positive-characteristic
field, and the labels agree with the cellular heads in this branch
([[lem-reduction-of-characteristic-zero-simple-modules-modulo-p]],
[[lem-positive-characteristic-specht-head-and-cyclotomic-crystal-labels-agree]]).

[F3] The adjustment polynomials are defined by
$[J(\nu)]=\sum_{\lambda}a_{\lambda,\nu}(q)[D(\lambda)]$, with $a_{\nu,\nu}=1$
and $a_{\lambda,\nu}=0$ unless $\lambda\unlhd\nu$
([[def-graded-adjustment-polynomials-in-positive-characteristic]]); the graded
Grothendieck group has the shift-orbit basis of the normalized simples, so all
expansions are unique
([[cor-graded-specht-classes-form-a-basis-of-the-module-grothendieck-group]]).
